g.text: Notes
3-D STATE (manifest itb.deviations_from_sheets, close-out r3) - centre-section
deck / fascia: roof_line(u) - crown_cap(u): 1.60 m below at the crown (deck
38.50), 0 at the notches (u +-27); profile 1.6 (1 - (u / 27)^2)^0.7 [obs photo
i4 (r1 / r2 re-measure), low]; the views draw: on roof_line(u) (crown 40.1)
3-D STATE (manifest itb.deviations_from_sheets, close-out r3) - centre-section
bottom chord: sagging bowstring: deck at the notches to WH + 2 at u = 0 [inf
(photos i3 / i4)]; the views draw: form unknown [unk]
The section is a measured roof top (NAIP eave profile anchored on the FAA DOF
roof tops) over an INFERRED structure: column positions from the published
spans, truss depth published as a maximum only.
Level 3 = DOF roof top minus "100 ft" (sfgate2000) / "90 ft" (Smith-Emery) /
the 83-ft hall height: 9.6-14.8 m, 11.5 adopted - no drawing or survey found.
West wall [inf]: the NAIP straight line fixes the wall only together with what
it images. The curb canopy (SEAONC: "760 tons of exposed steel at the ITB
departures level window walls and entrance canopy"; ~5 m above L3 and ~5 m
deep in photos) hides the wall's foot from the camera if deeper than ~2 m, so
the line is the canopy edge or the wall just above it: band v -28.3 to -23.3.
The earlier -26.3 (foot on L3) holds only for a canopy <= 2 m deep.
Hall width CONFLICT: 210 ft = 64.0 m [pub] against at most 61.0 m under the
roof east of the wall (55.9-61.0 over the band). Resolutions: the wall nearer
the eave; the hall continuing east under a lower roof (east edge = "fascia ->
lower roof fall"); a wider roof (SOM concept sketch 260 ft). Drawn: the
published width from the west wall (dashed), 5.5 m beyond the east eave.
